entries.text: std.logging · Source  logging.incn  """ Structured logging surface for ordinary Incan programs.  `std.logging` provides named logger values, level filtering, bound structured context, and human or JSON line output. Applications own logging configuration through `basic_config(...)`; libraries should acquire loggers and emit events without changing process policy.  Example:  ```incan from std.logging import Level, basic_config  def main() -> None:     basic_config(level=Level.INFO, target="stdout")     log.info("started") ``` """  from rust::std::io import stderr, stdout, Write from rust::std::string import String as RustString from std.datetime import DateTime from std.serde.json import Serialize from std.telemetry.core import (     Timestamp,     TelemetryValue,     Attributes,     Resource,     InstrumentationScope,     TraceId,     SpanId,     TraceFlags, )   pub enum Level(str):     """     Logging severity threshold and event level.      Levels are ordered from `TRACE` through `FATAL`. A configured threshold emits events at that level or any more     severe level.     """      TRACE = "TRACE"     DEBUG = "DEBUG"     INFO = "INFO"     WARN = "WARN"     ERROR = "ERROR"     FATAL = "FATAL"     WARNING = alias WARN     CRITICAL = alias FATAL      def rank(self) -> int:         """Return the ordering rank used by source-level threshold filtering."""         match self:             Level.TRACE => return 10             Level.DEBUG => return 20             Level.INFO => return 30             Level.WARN => return 40             Level.ERROR => return 50             Level.FATAL => return 60      def severity_number(self) -> int:         """Return the OpenTelemetry `SeverityNumber` for this level."""         match self:             Level.TRACE => return 1             Level.DEBUG => return 5             Level.INFO => return 9             Level.WARN => return 13             Level.ERROR => return 17             Level.FATAL => return 21      def display_name(self) -> str:         """Return the human-facing level name."""         match self:             Level.WARN => return "WARNING"             Level.FATAL => return "CRITICAL"             _ => return self.value()   pub enum LogFormat(str):     """     Event output format.      Use `HUMAN` for terminal-oriented text and `JSON` for one JSON object per emitted event.     """      HUMAN = "human"     JSON = "json"   pub enum LogStyle(str):     """     Human renderer style.      The style only affects `LogFormat.HUMAN`; JSON output keeps a stable record-shaped representation.     """      MINIMAL = "minimal"     SHORT = "short"     COMPLETE = "complete"     VERBOSE = "verbose"   pub enum ColorPolicy(str):     """     Human renderer color policy.      The policy is part of the committed configuration shape. The current source renderer is colorless until the stdlib     has a source-owned terminal capability surface.     """      AUTO = "auto"     ALWAYS = "always"     NEVER = "never"   @derive(Clone) pub type OutputTarget = newtype str:     """     Validated process stream for logging output.      `stdout` is useful for JSON line output that another process consumes. `stderr` keeps ordinary human logs separate     from application output and is the default target.     """      def from_underlying(target: str) -> Result[Self, ValidationError]:         """Validate and construct an output target."""         if target != "stdout" and target != "stderr":             return Err(ValidationError("std.logging target must be 'stdout' or 'stderr'"))         return Ok(OutputTarget(target))      def write_line(self, line: str) -> None:         """Write one rendered log line to the configured stream."""         data = RustString.from(line + "\n").into_bytes()         if self.0 == "stderr":             mut err = stderr()             _ = err.write_all(data)             return         mut out = stdout()         _ = out.write_all(data)   @derive(Clone) pub model LoggingConfig:     """     Source-level logging policy for the generated program.      Application entrypoints update this policy with `basic_config(...)`. Library code should leave it alone and only     emit events through `Logger` values.     """      pub level: Level = Level.WARN     pub format: LogFormat = LogFormat.HUMAN     pub style: LogStyle = LogStyle.SHORT     pub color: ColorPolicy = ColorPolicy.AUTO     pub target: OutputTarget = OutputTarget("stderr")   static _config: LoggingConfig = LoggingConfig()   pub model LogRecord with Serialize:     """     Structured event record produced by logger event methods.      Records use Incan field names and OpenTelemetry aliases. Event-specific attributes override bound logger     attributes with the same key.     """      pub timestamp [alias="Timestamp", description="Time when the event occurred."]: Timestamp     pub observed_timestamp [alias="ObservedTimestamp", description="Time when telemetry observed the event."]: Option[Timestamp] = None     pub trace_id [alias="TraceId", description="Request trace identifier when the event is span-correlated."]: Option[TraceId] = None     pub span_id [alias="SpanId", description="Span identifier when the event is span-correlated."]: Option[SpanId] = None     pub trace_flags [alias="TraceFlags", description="W3C trace flags for the correlated span."]: Option[TraceFlags] = None     pub severity_text [alias="SeverityText", description="OpenTelemetry severity text, such as INFO or WARN."]: str     pub severity_number [alias="SeverityNumber", description="OpenTelemetry normalized severity number."]: int     pub body [alias="Body", description="Human or structured event body."]: TelemetryValue     pub resource [alias="Resource", description="Entity that produced this telemetry."]: Resource     pub instrumentation_scope [alias="InstrumentationScope", description="Logical scope that emitted this record."]: InstrumentationScope     pub attributes [alias="Attributes", description="Additional structured attributes for this event."]: Attributes = Attributes(         {},     )     pub event_name [alias="EventName", description="Optional event class or type name."]: Option[str] = None      def emit(self, config: LoggingConfig) -> None:         """Render and write this record using the supplied logging policy."""         config.target.write_line(self._render_with(config.format, config.style))      def render(self, config: LoggingConfig) -> str:         """Render this record using the configured output format."""         return self._render_with(config.format, config.style)      def _render_with(self, format: LogFormat, style: LogStyle) -> str:         """Render this record using explicit format and style values."""         if format == LogFormat.JSON:             return self.to_json()         return self.render_human(style)      def render_human(self, style: LogStyle) -> str:         """Render this record with the configured human output style."""         rendered_level = self._level_display_name()         rendered_fields = self._attributes_human()         logger = self.instrumentation_scope.name         body = self.body.display_text()         match style:             LogStyle.MINIMAL => return f"[{rendered_level}] {body}{rendered_fields}"             LogStyle.SHORT => return f"{self._short_timestamp()} [{rendered_level}] {body}{rendered_fields}"             LogStyle.COMPLETE => return f"{self.timestamp.0} [{rendered_level}] {body}{rendered_fields}"             LogStyle.VERBOSE => return f"{self.timestamp.0} [{rendered_level}] {body}{rendered_fields}\n  logger={logger}"      def _short_timestamp(self) -> str:         if len(self.timestamp.0) >= 19:             return self.timestamp.0[11:19]         return self.timestamp.0      def _level_display_name(self) -> str:         match Level.from_value(self.severity_text):             Some(level) => return level.display_name()             None => return self.severity_text      def _attributes_human(self) -> str:         fields = self.attributes.0         if len(fields) == 0:             return ""          keys = sorted([key for key in fields.keys()])         return " fields={" + ", ".join([self._attribute_human(key, fields[key]) for key in keys]) + "}"      def _attribute_human(self, key: str, value: TelemetryValue) -> str:         return f"{key}=\"{value.display_text()}\""   @derive(Clone) pub type LoggerName = newtype str:     """     Validated dot-separated logger name.      Logger names must be non-empty, must not start or end with `.`, and must not contain empty path segments.     """      def from_underlying(name: str) -> Result[Self, ValidationError]:         """Validate and construct a logger name."""         if len(name) == 0:             return Err(ValidationError("std.logging logger names must not be empty"))         if name.startswith(".") or name.endswith("."):             return Err(ValidationError("std.logging logger names must not start or end with '.'"))         if name.contains(".."):             return Err(ValidationError("std.logging logger names must not contain empty segments"))         return Ok(LoggerName(name))   pub model Logger:     """     Named logger with bound structured context.      Logger values are cheap handles around a name and an immutable field map. Methods such as `bind(...)` and     `child(...)` return new loggers rather than mutating the original logger.     """      pub name: LoggerName     pub fields: Dict[str, TelemetryValue | str | bool | int | float | None] = {}      def child(self, suffix: str) -> Logger:         """         Return a descendant logger.          Args:             suffix: Dot-separated suffix to append to this logger's name.          Returns:             A logger named `<self.name>.<suffix>`.         """         return Logger(name=f"{self.name.0}.{suffix}", fields=self.fields)      def bind(self, fields: Dict[str, TelemetryValue | str | bool | int | float | None]) -> Logger:         """         Return a logger with additional bound context.
